title: Platform handoff playback and routing/auth quota sync - 2027-02-03
summary: Quick handoff + playback after last weekends quota throttle in EU and an auth token rotation that caused elevated 401s for a subset of dedicated customers. Goal: capture decisions, list follow-ups, and agree on short soak and rollout plan for the new router fallback policy.
notes: Incident background: Sat 02/01 03:20 UTC — quota controller misapplied soft limits for a customer segment in eu-west leading to request throttles. Autoscaler reacted but routing fallback rules did not kick for ~2m.
Auth rotation: key-rot pipeline completed Sat 02/01 02:45 UTC; a small wallet of dedicated deployments had an out-of-band KMS state and missed propagated token refresh, causing 401 spikes.
Observed impact: 2.7% request errors across eu-west for 10m, tail latency increase to 600ms p99 for 12m during retries and fallback attempts.

Root cause hypotheses discussed: mismatch in quota-controller feature flags across control-plane replicas; a race in rollout of routing rules; token refresh job not retrying on transient KMS timeouts.

Playback steps run in meeting: reproduced token rotation failure on staging with procmon logging; replayed quota controller with test harness and observed state drift when an older control-plane pod rejoined after cache refresh window.
Logs reviewed: truncated log excerpts from PLT-4328 showed 'quotaCache: staleEntry -> appliedSoftLimit' and router logs showed 'no-fallback-rule-matched' for 127 requests.
Customer impact note: two Dedicated customers experienced elevated 429/401 rates; CS already notified and provided a short RCA note. Follow-up CS checklist attached in linked_artifacts.
Temporal constraints: we want a low-risk fix deployed to prod by EOD Thu (02/05) with a staged canary to avoid reintroducing regressions ahead of next weekend traffic surge.
Observed mitigation already in place: manual replay of routing rules and emergency restart of stale control-plane replicas reduced throttles within 8 minutes during the original incident.

Quick wins identified: add conservative backoff and retry to token refresh pipeline, increase quota-controller cache reconciliation frequency during rollout windows, and add an explicit routing fallback match for queued requests when policies mismatch.
Longer-term: investigate quorum-based feature-flag rollout and add vector tests for control-plane replica rejoin scenarios in the chaos-harness.
Cross-team asks: Security to confirm KMS telemetry; SRE to own increased reconciliation experiment; Product to approve customer-facing wording for the RCA.
Risks noted: toggling cache reconciliation too aggressively could increase DB load; routing fallback change must be size-limited and tested on small Dedicates first.

Decision: implement two-phase fix: (1) patch token-refresh retry + observability (small PR), (2) routing fallback rule change gated behind a canary (feature-flag), (3) temporary reconciliation frequency bump for the rollout window only.
action_items: Lucas: open PR for token-refresh retry + metrics (aim: PR by 02/04, deploy to staging 02/05). Link in linked_artifacts.
Priya: schedule a 48hr reconciliation bump on quota-controller for the rollout window; monitor DB RPS. Start time: 02/05 12:00 UTC. Create alert if DB CPU > 70%.
Diego: implement routing fallback feature-flag and small canary (5% of traffic in eu-west). Work with release-engineering for controlled rollout. Target: canary ready 02/06.
Maya: validate KMS health dashboard and add a token-rotation success metric; confirm KMS retry recommendations (expected done 02/05).
Jordan (on-call): run the canary monitor playbook during initial rollout; escalate to platform pager if 5xx or error increase >1% over baseline.
Asha: coordinate customer communications draft with CS and legal; aim to publish an interim note after patch deploy and a full RCA after postmortem (draft by 02/06).
All: add 15m follow-up sync 02/06 09:30 UTC to sign-off canary results and decide final rollout schedule.
Follow-up ticket: consolidate short-term mitigation tasks under JIRA PLT-4401 (Priya to own).
decisions: Apply token-refresh retry + enhanced metrics immediately to staging and prod after validation (low risk).
Gate routing fallback policy change behind feature-flag + 5% canary in eu-west before wider rollout.
Do not change global reconciliation frequency permanently; apply temporary bump during the rollout window only and revert after 48h post-rollout if stable.
CS will send an interim customer note post-patch, legal to review wording.
metrics_and_observations: Pre-incident baseline: eu-west p99 latency ~280ms, error rate ~0.12%
Incident peak: p99 ~600ms, error rate peaked 2.7% (mostly 401/429), total impacted requests ~11.6k
Current staging soak: token-refresh retry lowered reproduced 401s from 18/100 to 1/100 in synthetic test harness
DB RPS with temporary reconciliation bump in testing +18% (SRE watching CPU and connection pools)
Canary threshold for failure: >1% increase in error rate or >15% increase in p99 latency triggers rollback.
blockers: Need legal sign-off on customer-facing language for interim note — blocking publication of customer communication until EOD 02/05.
Release-engineering calendar constraint: major infra patch scheduled 02/07 which limits date windows for full rollout.
Limited dedicated envs for canary verification for specific enterprise customers; may need opt-in approach.
next_meeting: 2027-02-06 09:30 UTC (15m) - canary sign-off; invite: platform-engineering, on-call, CS rep, security. Agenda: canary metrics, decision to expand rollout or rollback.
notes_to_self: Capture the small log query used for reproducing stale cache: "SELECT id, version, last_seen FROM quota_cache WHERE last_seen < now() - interval '2m'" and add to runbook. Put token-rotation playbook on the runbook index under 'auth/token-refresh'.
